run.question: Can you see any issues in recent logs for traffic-manager deployment in namespace app-102b

report.summary: The traffic-manager Deployment in namespace app-102b is a freshly created nginx:latest workload (created 2026-11-21T05:18:55Z, observedGeneration 1, 3/3 ready, Available and Progressing both True) whose three pods came up cleanly and whose own container stdout contains only nginx startup lines. The only issue visible in recent logs is a single ERROR line at 2026-11-21T05:18:58Z on pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-8kl8r: {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"}. In the sampled window it is the only error-level line in the whole job="nginx" stream and the only occurrence of that message, so 1 of 151 log lines in the namespace is an error and the other two pods logged none. The log's memory claim is not corroborated by anything I could see: the pod template sets no resource requests or limits at all (resources: {}), no container has restarted and none has a last-termination reason, and the only node reports MemoryPressure=False. Prometheus was unreachable during this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on all metric queries) and the Services query returned nothing, so error-rate, memory-usage and Service/endpoint corroboration are missing. No fault-injection or other triggering object was found in the namespace (its only ConfigMap is kube-root-ca.crt), so no root cause object can be named.

claims.text: Deployment traffic-manager in namespace app-102b exists with spec.replicas 3, status.readyReplicas 3, image nginx:latest, and conditions Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable) at observedGeneration 1.

The Deployment and its single ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 (revision 1) were created at 2026-11-21T05:18:55Z, and the three pods traffic-manager-585c5579f6-8kl8r, -rfb4s and -xg7rr are Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination state, startTime 2026-11-21T05:18:55Z.

Namespace app-102b events in the window are all Normal and start at 05:18:55Z: Deployment traffic-manager "Scaled up replica set traffic-manager-585c5579f6 from 0 to 3", followed by three ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate events and per-pod Scheduled/Pulling/Pulled/Created/Started for nginx:latest; there are no FailedScheduling, BackOff, Unhealthy, Killing or Evicted events for this workload.

The only error line in recent logs is on pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-8kl8r at 2026-11-21T05:18:58Z: {"level":"ERROR","message":"Memory alert","error":"Memory requests above 90%, consider adding more memory","status":501,"request_id":"req-a]8f2c1d4"} (Loki labels namespace=app-102b, pod=traffic-manager-585c5579f6-8kl8r, job=nginx, level=ERROR).

Loki counts for the sampled window: 50 lines for pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-8kl8r with no level label, 50 for -rfb4s, 50 for -xg7rr, plus exactly 1 line with level=ERROR on -8kl8r (151 lines total in namespace app-102b, all timestamped between 05:18:57.001Z and 05:18:58Z); the error-level count for job="nginx" across all namespaces returns exactly one series, app-102b / traffic-manager-585c5579f6-8kl8r = 1.

The remaining 150 Loki lines are INFO "HTTP request completed" entries (for example GET /api/v1/orders status 200/201, GET /api/v1/users, GET /api/v1/products, GET /api/v1/inventory, GET /health with response_time_ms between about 50 and 199 ms) across all three pods, i.e. most requests succeeded and only the single 501 error was recorded.

Container stdout read from the pods via the kubelet contains only 23 nginx startup lines per pod (docker-entrypoint.sh, configuration complete, nginx/1.31.9 worker start) for -8kl8r at 05:18:57.63-57.68Z, -rfb4s at 05:18:56.81-56.86Z and -xg7rr at 05:18:57.23-57.28Z, with no previous container instance available and no error text.

The pod template of traffic-manager sets no resources (containers[0].resources is {} with image nginx:latest, no probes, no env, no configMap/secret mounts), so a message about "memory requests above 90%" is not explained by any request or limit configured on this workload.

The only node, opspilot-m1-control-plane, reports MemoryPressure=False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory ("kubelet has sufficient memory available") and 32859944Ki allocatable memory at the time of the query, and the pods show restartCount 0 with no last termination state, so neither node memory pressure nor an OOM kill is visible for this workload.

Namespace app-102b contains only one ConfigMap, kube-root-ca.crt (created 2026-11-21T05:18:55Z, holding only the cluster CA bundle), so no fault-injection, delay or failure setting is present in that namespace's ConfigMaps.

The cluster-wide event grouping for the window contains no Pod reason (BackOff, Unhealthy, Killing, Evicted, Failed) or other event involving the traffic-manager pods; the app-102b entries in the grouping are Deployment ScalingReplicaSet 1, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate 3 and Pod Created/Pulled/Pulling/Scheduled/Started 3 each.

The "Memory alert" ERROR with status 501 is a single application-emitted event on pod traffic-manager-585c5579f6-8kl8r rather than a cluster-level memory shortage, because no memory request is configured on the pod, the container never restarted, and the node reports no MemoryPressure; the actual stimulus behind it (application-side threshold logic, an injected/synthetic log source, or genuine container memory use) is not determinable without metrics.

The Loki lines labeled job="nginx", pod=traffic-manager-585c5579f6-* are not identical to what the same pods' containers wrote to stdout: the kubelet log view holds only the 23 nginx startup lines up to 05:18:57.68Z, while Loki holds 150 JSON "HTTP request completed" lines plus the ERROR line for the same pods in the same second, so the JSON access/error lines may come from a separate log source/shipper rather than this nginx container's own output.

Set explicit CPU/memory requests and limits (and a readiness probe) on the traffic-manager container, since the log line complains about memory requests while the pod template has resources: {} and no probes.

Re-check the 501 / "Memory alert" occurrence with working metrics (container memory working set vs requests, HTTP 5xx rate) and confirm whether a Service selects the app=nginx pods, since Prometheus was unreachable and the Services query returned no items in this Run.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for this Run: metrics_range_query for kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace="app-102b"} and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace="app-102b"} and instant queries for kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace="app-102b"} and kube_pod_container_resource_requests{namespace="app-102b"} all returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so memory usage, request-vs-usage ratio, restart counters and error-rate series for traffic-manager are unknown, not zero.

The Services query for namespace app-102b returned status no_data (no items), so whether traffic-manager is exposed by a Service and whether its endpoints match the app=nginx pods is unknown, and ingress/endpoint misconfiguration cannot be ruled out or confirmed.

Loki shows only about one second of log history (05:18:57.001Z-05:18:58Z) for this namespace and the pods and Deployment were created at 05:18:55Z, so there is no earlier baseline for these pods; the log stream before 05:18:57Z is unknown, not clean.

Whether the "Memory alert" / 501 line was caused by real container memory consumption, by application threshold logic, or by a synthetic log source could not be verified: the kubelet container logs of the same pod contain no such JSON line, and no metric corroboration was obtainable.

Kubernetes events for namespace app-102b cover only 05:18:55Z-05:18:57Z, so earlier activity in that namespace (and the period before the Deployment existed) is unknown; event history before that point was not available.

No change-history integration is available in this Run, so who or what created the Deployment at 2026-11-21T05:18:55Z and whether any configuration was applied to it cannot be determined from the authorized sources.
next_steps: Restore/verify Prometheus scrape access and re-run container memory working-set vs requests, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and HTTP 5xx rate queries for namespace app-102b over the incident window.
Check whether a Service (and any Ingress) exists for traffic-manager with selector app=nginx and that its Endpoints contain the three pod IPs.
Watch the traffic-manager pods for recurrence of status 501 / "Memory alert" and collect later logs, since the current evidence covers only the first ~1 second of pod lifetime.
Confirm with the change-history owner what created the traffic-manager Deployment and ReplicaSet traffic-manager-585c5579f6 at 2026-11-21T05:18:55Z.
Review whether the Loki job="nginx" stream is fed by this nginx container or by a separate log source, to decide how much weight the JSON log lines should carry.
